stemMd: A single-base substitution changes an mRNA codon but leaves the encoded amino acid unchanged. Which property makes this possible?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Every codon specifies several amino acids simultaneously.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Several codons can specify the same amino acid.

options.label: E
options.textMd: All substitutions occur outside coding regions.

explanationMd: The genetic code is degenerate: more than one codon may encode a given amino acid. A substitution between such codons is synonymous, so sequence change need not change the polypeptide.

distractorRationale.a: Some third-position substitutions change the encoded amino acid.
distractorRationale.e: The stem specifies a codon change.
distractorRationale.c: The code is degenerate, not ordinarily ambiguous in that way.
